newsitem.title: GERMANY: Costcutting lifts Bayernwerk 96 oper profit.
newsitem.headline: Costcutting lifts Bayernwerk 96 oper profit.

text.p: Eletricity group Bayernwerk AG on Wednesday reported a 13 percent rise in 1996 operating profit to 1.66 billion marks, and said 1997 should be equally good.
Bayernwerk's management board chairman Otto Majewski said 1996, the company's 75th anniversary year, had ended very successfully and said he expected "similarly good" operating earnings in 1997.

The Viag unit's chief financial officer Manfred Klis said he was confident earnings would improve as up to 500 million marks in cost benefits from a group-wide restructuring programme fed into the bottom-line.

However, Bayernwerk saw a sharp decline in group net profit to 659 million marks in calendar 1996 from 768 million in 1997, which the group said was mainly because the previous year's figure had contained tax benefits and extraordinary earnings of 388 million marks.
The electricity giant said it expected a positive effect on earnings from synergies arising from the purchase of power company Isar-Amperwerke.
German cartel authorities approved the takeover of Isar-Amperwerke at the end of May.
Bayernwerk said it expected losses in its fledgling telecommunications business to continue as it invested in the sector.
Group sales in 1996 grew to 9.5 billion marks from 9.2 billion marks, which Bayernwerk said was mainly due to the first-time consolidation of gas company Thueringen.
The group said it planned to split its activities in the energy market into individual stand-alone profit centres during 1998.
Bayernwerk's power production, distribution, power sales and marketing divisions are set to each become independent profit centres, management board chairman Otto Majewski said in a speech.

One holding company would focus on common objectives and developing new areas. The holding company would also deal with the central coordination of network load, electricity production, sales and distribution.
Bayernwerk AG also said that it had set aside reserves of 8.4 billion marks for the disposal of nuclear waste and for the future mothballing of nuclear plants.
In 1995 the Viag subsidiary allowed for 8.3 billion marks in reserves for the same purpose.
Earlier this year Bayernwerk spoke out against the possible introduction of legislation aimed at taxing the reserves set aside for shutting down their nuclear plants.
